title: The instruction has no row and no published operation in rwb-litigation, and the partner rows and the pack are other services'
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-009, story, data table, endpoints table); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md rows FEAT-LIT-09 and FEAT-PRM-02; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.9; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T3.1, T5.2 and T-A.1; _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4: 2 tables, 5 operations, 0 events, 0 jobs, 1 workflow)
section: RWB-S4-E5009-APP sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8, 13, 19; RWB-S4-E5009-CON sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 (AC2, AC3), 8 (BR3, BR4, BR11), 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8, 13, 19; the metadata rows and the two fragments
description: Four values the step needs are fixed by no source. (1) The home of the instruction: the legacy data table names partner (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007) and partner_instruction (DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016), but the ownership rows of rwb-litigation name only hearing and legal_action, so both rows belong to the partner-management service and no Ownership Map row for them is in the pack. (2) The pack: the legacy story says the instruction carries the pack, the pack items are document rows of P5 and no pack element is published for the instruction. (3) The operation: no source names an operation of the partner portal for the instruction, although the FSD gives the integration point as Partner portal and the TSD names no interface for it. (4) The instruction fields: the legacy table names six fields of the eleven the instruction needs and no source names the rest. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the step needs only its own contract and the two platform contracts.
evidence: Context pack: 'Tables (2) hearing, legal_action', 'REST operations provided (5) GET and PATCH /legal-actions/{legalActionId}, POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions, POST /legal-actions/{legalActionId}/hearings, POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve', 'Events (0)', 'Jobs (0)', 'Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow'. TSD S4 T3.1 gives legal_action 14 fields and hearing 6, none of them an instruction; T-A.1 gives the five operations above and no instruction operation; T5.2 says only 'P3 for the case, P7 for the decision log, P4 for access and reference data, P5 for documents, P6 for notices'. The legacy data table names recovery_case, timer, partner, partner_instruction, decision_log_entry and rule_row; the legacy endpoints table names POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions and GET /legal-actions/{legalActionId}. Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3: FEAT-LIT-09 systems 'Partner portal, LIT'; FEAT-LIT-08 depends on FEAT-PRM-02, the S9 panel. Architecture v5 slides 4 and 8 in the context pack: partner management S9 rwb-partner, partner gateway FAPI 2.0.
area: Application and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with S9 rwb-partner and P5 rwb-document
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the S9 rwb-partner and P5 rwb-document architects
proposed: Carry the legacy sentences unchanged with their origin tags and record the target reading: the instruction is composed here, the partner and partner_instruction rows stay with rwb-partner and are read or requested on its contract (operation name left as the placeholder), the pack travels as document references read on API-P5-002, this service writes no business row and no document, and the two provided operations remain API-S4-002 and API-S4-003 of the legacy endpoints block.

title: The firm events are named in the rules while the service publishes and consumes nothing, and the case answer has no operation name
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-24, R-LIT-26 and R-LIT-28 (event column FIRM_MATCHED, FIRM_NOMINATED, FIRM_BREACHED_SLA); _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows: Events (0); Temporal and Drools slides that name this service); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.9.4.4 (system background events None); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T4, T5.2 and T5.3
section: RWB-S4-E5009-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.8, 13; RWB-S4-E5009-CON sections 2, 3, 7 (AC4, AC6), 8 (BR5), 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 19; the events_published and events_consumed keys of both fragments
description: Two readings of the trigger collide. The Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 names an event for each of the three rules and the state machine of the TSD gives the same names, which reads as an event or a message on a topic. Against that, the ownership rows of rwb-litigation give the service zero events, the FSD declares no system background event for the feature, and DP-09 (outbox and inbox) and DP-14 (topic naming) are not in the pattern set of this key, so the service has no inbox, no consumer group and no published event to name. Separately, the answer that asks rwb-case to move the case, to start the case-stage timer and to raise the task has no operation name in any source: TSD S4 T5.2 says only 'P3 for the case'.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 lines 163, 165 and 167: R-LIT-24 event FIRM_MATCHED, R-LIT-26 FIRM_NOMINATED, R-LIT-28 FIRM_BREACHED_SLA, each with systems 'Partner Portal'. TSD S4 T4 lists the same three rules with the same from and to states. Context pack ownership rows: 'Events (0) - None'. FSD S4 A2.9.4.4: 'None - No background event'. TSD S4 T5.3: 'Events - None'. The metadata rows of both stories carry Contract, Integration and External dependencies None, and the patterns applied are DP03, DP13 and DP19 only.
area: Integration and trigger design, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case and S9 rwb-partner
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case and S9 rwb-partner architects and the event platform team
proposed: Read FIRM_MATCHED, FIRM_NOMINATED and FIRM_BREACHED_SLA as the names of workflow signals and not as Kafka subscriptions: the firm arrives on the workflow signal of the selection step, the firm facts are read on the P9 contract and the case stage is answered on the rwb-case contract, both one hop with a 2 s budget, and neither story publishes or consumes an event. Name the case read when the rwb-case contract story is written and leave the metadata rows as the plan gives them.

title: The partner clock of 2 working days has no stated home, and the working-day calendar and instruction types have no value in any source
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-24, R-LIT-26 and R-LIT-28 (timer column 2 working days and None); _work/msr/context/S4.md (Jobs (0); Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow; Temporal and Drools slide 7 notes); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E5-009 data table (timer, DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T3.2, T5.3 and T6
description: The legacy story starts a partner clock when the instruction is issued and its data table names a timer row, which in the target is P3's table. The pack gives rwb-litigation no job and one workflow, so the clock can only be a durable timer of LitigationWorkflow, but no source states that the partner clock belongs to S4 rather than to the case or the partner service. Its measurement is worse: 2 working days is a duration in a working-day calendar, no source names the calendar, the holidays or the instruction window that the partner holds, and the instruction types the portal accepts are a list that no source publishes. R-LIT-28's expiry path is also split: the breach mark is the partner service's row, the task is the case service's and the re-selection is the firm-selection story's.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-24 and R-LIT-26 timer column '2 working days', R-LIT-28 'None', action 'Mark the instruction breached, notify the partner manager and re-select', to state FIRM_DECLINED. Context pack: 'Jobs (0) - None', 'Workflows (1) - LitigationWorkflow'; Temporal and Drools slide 7: 'Temporal keeps the dates' and 'Law firm chosen by rule, instructed'. Legacy data table: 'timer | id, case_id, task_id, timer_type, started_at, expires_at and 4 more | DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036'. FSD S4 A2.9.3.1 gives R-LIT-28 and BR-S4-009 'No value a business person may change is written in code; it is read from reference data with its version'. TSD S4 T3.2 lists LOV-LEGAL-TYPE and no instruction-window list, and T6 gives no scheduler.
area: Workflow and reference data, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case and S9 rwb-partner
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case and S9 rwb-partner architects and the business owner of the partner service levels
proposed: Declare the partner clock as one durable timer of LitigationWorkflow of 2 working days started at instructed_at, measured on a working-day calendar read as a versioned reference row whose content is the placeholder; fire R-LIT-28 on expiry, answer FIRM_BREACHED_SLA to rwb-case with the partner-and-agency-manager task, mark the breach on the P9 contract and leave the re-selection to the firm-selection story; keep the case-stage timer and the task rows with rwb-case.

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-009, so both stories trace to the feature and to REQ-S4-004
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-009 (metadata table rows Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-09, Process, Priority, Depends on FEAT-LIT-08, Decision - no requirement row); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json entry RWB-E5-009 with reqs = []; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md Requirements served (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010)
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories and the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-009 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-09 and the prerequisite FEAT-LIT-08 and no requirement row, the run's legacy index records an empty requirement list, and the Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the feature one row and no requirement. The FSD S4 requirements table has no requirement that names the instruction alone; the nearest is REQ-S4-004, 'A law firm is selected from the panel by rule using panel performance, and instructed through the partner portal', which covers both the selection of the predecessor and this instruction. Both stories therefore trace to FEAT-LIT-09 and to REQ-S4-004 with the reading stated, and the PRD column carries the placeholder until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD of the module adds an identifier.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-009 has seven rows and no requirement row; the legacy index records reqs: [] for the key; FSD S4 v3 'Requirements served' lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 and only REQ-S4-004 names the instruction; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row for FEAT-LIT-09 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind System, primary role 'Runs unattended', systems 'Partner portal, LIT', depends on FEAT-LIT-08 and no requirement.
area: Traceability and requirements, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst, S4 rwb-litigation, with the PRD owner of EP05
proposed: Add one requirement row to the Epics 3 to 8 PRD and to the S4 module trace covering the firm instruction as its own requirement, and rewrite the requirement column of both stories and of their fragments when it exists; until then keep REQ-S4-004 with the reading stated in section 18.

title: The rule package that decides the three rules is a consumed contract of another service with no dependency row and no pattern in the set
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md R-LIT-24, R-LIT-26, R-LIT-28; _work/msr/context/S4.md (DP table row DP-04 and the rule governance block of Temporal and Drools slide 11); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.9.3.1; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5009-APP and RWB-S4-E5009-CON (Contract dependencies None; patterns DP03, DP13, DP19)
section: RWB-S4-E5009-APP sections 3, 4, 8, 12.2, 12.8, 13 and 19; RWB-S4-E5009-CON sections 3, 7 (AC6), 8 (BR12), 12.2, 12.8 and 19
description: The step cannot decide anything without the LITIGATION package of rwb-decision at its version in force, because the three rules and their conditions are rows of that package. In the target the package is authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and the runtime is embedded per service, which the DP table carries as DP-04 with H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON. DP-04 is not in the pattern set of this key, no such platform or service contract story is in the dependencies the plan gives this slice, and the metadata rows say Contract dependencies None, so the package read is a consumed contract that no row declares.
evidence: Context pack DP table: 'DP-04 embedded Drools + rule packages from rwb-decision', full table row 'DP-04 ... H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON'; Temporal and Drools slide 11: 'RULE GOVERNANCE (rwb-decision, P7) Rule models + central ledger, approve, publish EV-30, seal decision records'. FSD S4 A2.9.3.1 gives R-LIT-24, R-LIT-26, R-LIT-28 and BR-S4-009 'read from reference data with its version'. The patterns of both stories are DP03, DP13 and DP19; the dependency rows of both stories are None except the app story's three H rows.
area: Dependency map and rule governance, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision and the platform rule kit
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P7 rwb-decision architect and the platform rule-kit owner
proposed: Carry the package read as a non-blocking consumed row on rwb-decision's contract with its fake, keep the metadata rows as the plan gives them, and record DP-04 with its two contracts in the Dependency Map when the rule-governance keys are realigned; the embedded runtime stays a service-template capability and no rule row is authored in this key.
